terms.meaning: The distance from the Sun at which water can stay liquid. It is also called the Goldilocks zone.
Gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat from the Earth’s surface and keep the planet warm.
A layer in the atmosphere that stops harmful ultraviolet rays.
All living things, interacting with the air, water and land.
Reproduction from a single parent, giving copies of it.
A reproductive cell that carries half of the parent’s genetic material.
The cell formed when male and female gametes join at fertilisation.

items.name: Hottest planet
items.formula: Venus, at about 450 °C, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.

items.name: Size and gravity
items.formula: Earth’s gravity holds the atmosphere without crushing living things.
items.example: Mercury and Mars are too small to hold much atmosphere.

items.name: Magnetic field
items.formula: It shields the Earth from high-energy particles.
items.example: These particles would otherwise harm life.

items.name: Four spheres
items.formula: Atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere and biosphere work together.
items.example: Water covers about 70% of the surface, so about 30% is land.

items.name: Vegetative propagation
items.formula: New plants grow from roots, stems or leaves.
items.example: Potato eyes, ginger buds and Bryophyllum leaves.

items.name: Simple animals and microbes
items.formula: Amoeba and bacteria divide in two. Hydra forms buds. Planaria regrows from a piece.
items.example: All of these need just one parent.

items.name: Why gametes carry half
items.formula: So the zygote has a complete set of genes, half from each parent.
items.example: This is why siblings differ a little.

items.name: Parts of a flower
items.formula: Male: anther with pollen, on a filament. Female: stigma, style and ovary.

items.name: Pollination and fertilisation
items.formula: Pollen moves from anther to stigma. Then gametes join in the ovule.
items.example: The ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.

items.name: Young in different animals
items.formula: Fish and frogs: outside the body, in water. Birds and reptiles: lay shelled eggs. Mammals: develop inside the mother.
items.example: A hen lays eggs, while a cow gives birth to a calf.

items.name: Climate change
items.formula: Burning fossil fuels adds greenhouse gases and warms the planet.
items.example: Ice caps melt and sea levels rise.

items.name: Biodiversity loss and pollution
items.formula: Habitat loss and polluted air, water and soil harm life.
items.example: Plastic waste and factory waste harm rivers.

items.name: Montreal Protocol
items.formula: A 1987 agreement to phase out the chemicals that damage the ozone layer.

items.name: Paris Agreement
items.formula: A 2015 agreement that countries would cut greenhouse gases to limit warming.
items.example: Its goal is to keep warming below 1.5 °C.

mistakes.text: A greenhouse gas does not work like a glasshouse, which traps warm air. The gas absorbs heat radiated by the Earth.
The greenhouse effect is not all bad. Without it the Earth would be frozen.
The planet nearest the Sun is not the hottest. Venus is hotter than Mercury.
The ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit. Do not swap them.
